title: Gentle Landing & Garden Therapy
description: You land at 13:55 — by the time you clear customs and reach your hotel, it'll be late afternoon. Today is all about gentle acclimatization: check in, stretch your legs in one of Tokyo's most beautiful gardens, and end with a comforting vegetarian dinner.

activities.title: Haneda Airport → Shinjuku
activities.description: Take Keikyu Line to Shinagawa, then JR Yamanote Line to Shinjuku (~50 min, ¥600). Or the Limousine Bus direct to Shinjuku (¥1,400, no transfers).
details: 🧳 Pick up Suica/Pasmo at the airport (¥500 deposit + load ¥3,000-5,000)
💡 Grab an ekiben at Haneda — inari sushi or vegetable tempura boxes are safe bets

activities.title: Check In & Freshen Up
activities.description: Drop bags at your Shinjuku accommodation. Budget options: Imano Tokyo Hostel (¥4,000-6,000/night, private rooms), Unplan Shinjuku, or Citadines (apartment-style with kitchen for self-catering).
details: 💡 A kitchen or fridge helps with vegetarian meal prep

tips.text: 🕐 Don't fight jetlag too hard — stay awake until 20:00-21:00 and you'll reset faster. Walk slowly, hydrate, avoid napping.

activities.title: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
activities.description: 10-minute walk from Shinjuku Station, this 144-acre garden is the perfect jetlag antidote. Three distinct gardens: Japanese (zen ponds), English (wide lawns), and French (formal). Late April means wisteria beginning to bloom in the pergolas.
details: 📷 Taiwan Pavilion and greenhouse are hidden gems

meals.name: Ain Soph. Journey — Shinjuku
meals.description: Tokyo's most beloved vegan restaurant. Heavenly Vegan Burger or seasonal tofu steak set meal. Everything labeled, staff speaks English, cozy interior feels like a warm hug after a long flight.

tips.text: Ain Soph Journey is genuinely one of the best vegan spots in Tokyo — the burger and pancakes are a must. Even non-vegan Japanese friends love it.
🌙 After dinner, stroll Shinjuku's neon streets — Kabukicho's Godzilla Head is minutes away.
